newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold futures end weaker, PGMs mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold futures end weaker, PGMs mostly higher.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures ended mixed on Monday, with gold and silver mostly lower while platinum group metals (PGMs) settled mostly higher amid lingering concern over Russia's PGM sales, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from unchanged to four yen per gram lower. Benchmark April was ended four yen off at 1,244 yen.
"Although the yen retreated against the dollar, weaker spot gold prices dragged gold futures lower toward the close," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
Bullion was quoted at $337.20/60 per ounce at 0719 GMT, against $337.40/90 in New York on Friday.

"Producer selling dented spot gold during Asian hours, and more falls are likely," one trader said. "Sentiment is bearish sentiment due to possible sales by European central banks and private investors are unlikely to build fresh longs unless benchmark April falls below 1,200 yen," the trader said.

In PGMs, prices were lifted by the extremely high lease rates due to absence of Russian sales and short-covering from private investors ahead of the spot contract expiry on Wednesday, the traders said.
Traders here speculated that the resumption of Russian PGM sales would be be behind the initial schedule.
The Russian platinum group metal export agency previously told Japanese clients it would resume spot sales in late June, but no signs of Russian sales have appeared yet, traders said.
Palladium futures ranged from four yen per gram lower to 25 yen up, with benchmark April off four yen at 525 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from two yen to 29 yen per gram higher. Benchmark April platinum was up two yen at 1,359 yen.
Benchmark April silver was off 0.1 yen per 10 grams at 177.2 yen. --Tokyo Commodities Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
